### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. congenital bilateral aplasia of vas deferens from CFTR mutation  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.781)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:1884)

**Proposed mechanism:** CFTR (HGNC:2408) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial ion transport (GO:0007049); Epithelial ion transport (GO:0007049) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital bilateral aplasia of vas deferens (HP:0000027); Epithelial ion transport (GO:0007049) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens (HP:0000027); Epithelial ion transport (GO:0007049) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal sweat chloride concentration (HP:0003574); Epithelial ion transport (GO:0007049) —LEADS_TO→ Pancreatic insufficiency (HP:0002030). Loss-of-function mutations in CFTR disrupt epithelial ion transport, leading to a spectrum of phenotypes including congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (common to both diseases) and other manifestations like abnormal sweat chloride concentration and pancreatic insufficiency.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in CFTR that are exclusively associated with only one of the two diseases, despite being predicted to cause loss-of-function. _(variant: rs75721044)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis of these conditions can inform therapeutic strategies targeting CFTR function, potentially benefiting patients with either disease.
